title: NPCI postpones 0.4% UPI merchant fee after retailer pushback
body: NPCI put off a planned October 15 rollout of a 0.4% fee on eligible UPI merchant transactions above ₹2,000. The stated reason was the festive shopping season, and the fee will now start after Diwali with no new date given. The page says the delay followed "broad pushback from merchants across the country". Transactions of ₹2,000 or less and small merchants receiving under ₹100,000 a month via UPI were to be exempt, and fees on larger payments were capped at ₹300. Retailers and petrol pump operators opposed the fee, and some warned they could stop accepting UPI. Banks and payment firms say they need a way to recover network costs.

title: IndiGo CEO says 'no choice' but to raise fares further as fuel bill jumps
body: After IndiGo's July-September results, CEO Willie Walsh said, "We have no choice but to look to increase fares", citing fuel costs. The airline reported a consolidated net loss of ₹1,879.1 crore, its third straight quarterly loss, with fuel expenditure up 67.2% to ₹9,966.8 crore. Passengers carried fell 4.7% to about 2.75 crore, while passenger yield rose to ₹6.30 per km from ₹4.69. Fuel surcharges are already in place, and the company says it has recovered about 60% of the fuel cost increase. The page does not quote passenger reactions, but the figures show flyers are already paying more per km.

title: FMCG firms shrink packs and may raise prices after Diwali
body: Companies have cut pack sizes to absorb rising input costs, but there is little room left on low-price items such as Parle-G's Rs 10 pack. HUL took increases of about 7.5% in the September quarter, and Tata Consumer raised tea prices 8-10%. Plastic packaging costs were reported 30-40% higher in October 2026, palm oil rose 21% year on year in September, and cocoa rose 48%. Experts expect firms to pass costs on after the festive season. They warn that visible hikes could push shoppers to rival brands, that shrinkflation is now more visible on social media, and that lower-income households are hit hardest.

title: Amazon Great Indian Festival: premium phones up 50%, EMI spend up 40%
body: Amazon reports a 50% year-on-year rise in shopping volume, with over 70% of shoppers from non-metro markets. Android phones above ₹30,000 grew 50%, premium smartwatches grew fivefold, and 55-inch and larger screens made up 60% of TV purchases. EMI spending rose 40%, with nearly 90% of it through No-Cost EMI. Amazon says customers saved over ₹2,800 crore, and daily Amazon Now orders grew 18 times. These are company-reported figures, and the sale runs through Bhai Dooj on November 11. The page gives no independent view of what shoppers think.

title: Dhanteras: gold falls from peak, jewellers expect flat volumes
body: Ahead of Dhanteras on November 6, jewellers expect better sentiment but sales volumes to stay largely flat year on year. Sales value is forecast to rise 15-30%. Gold peaked at Rs 1,62,900 on May 29, fell Rs 20,900 (12.8%) to Rs 1,42,000 on October 31, and was Rs 1,46,600 on Wednesday. Silver has corrected by nearly 50%, and the industry expects silver volumes to rise 10%. Kama Jewelry expects volumes to fall about 10%. The Gem and Jewellery Council's vice chairman said the Prime Minister's appeal to avoid buying gold had affected demand. Shoppers are shifting toward lighter pieces and silver.

title: Zomato's 'Have a WOW Diwali' ad with Saif Ali Khan gets a lukewarm review
body: Zomato's in-house Diwali film stars Saif Ali Khan receiving unwanted gifts such as a shaving kit, soap and a protein supplement flavoured with soan papdi. A delivery partner then brings a restaurant food hamper, which he praises. The aim is to promote curated hampers from restaurant partners. The reviewer calls it funny and well cast but predictable, says the hamper gets little demonstration, and says the rejected gifts are more interesting than the product. A marketing professor quoted says an ad that only confirms expectations makes surprise harder. The page lists this date as the last-updated time, and it shows no public reaction numbers.

title: Swiggy Instamart leans on discounts again; stock hits record low
body: In the September quarter, discounts including brand-funded ones were 29% of Instamart's order value, up from 26% in June. About 100 basis points of gross order value went into targeted investments, including a Rs 9 store and customer-group-specific pricing, to win back lapsed users. Instamart's adjusted EBITDA loss widened to Rs 895 crore from Rs 778 crore. Blinkit's net order value grew 79% year on year to Rs 20,940 crore versus 35% for Instamart. Swiggy says losses peaked this quarter and plans an inventory-led model. The page is investor-focused, so shopper sentiment is not covered.

title: Navratri auto retail: 11.23 lakh units, down 6.52% against last year
body: FADA's provisional data for October 11-20 shows 11,23,086 vehicles sold, up 26.76% from 2024 but down 6.52% from the 11-day 2025 period. Passenger vehicles were 1,82,728 units, up 10.39% on 2024 but down 21.91% on 2025. Two-wheelers were 8,34,075 units, down 2.79% on 2025. Electric vehicles reached 1,17,437 units, about 10.46% of registrations, and electric two-wheelers rose 33.41% on 2025. FADA blamed much of the drop against 2025 on calendar differences, since last year's festive period was longer and coincided with GST 2.0. The page does not report buyer reactions.

title: September auto retail hits 25.37 lakh units, but FADA says low base inflates it
body: FADA data shows September retail of 25,36,920 units, up 31.82% year on year. Two-wheelers were 17,90,188 units (+33.08%) and passenger vehicles 4,27,213 units (+32.10%). EV retail was about 3.34 lakh units, roughly 13% penetration. FADA says the jump is inflated by a low base, because many buyers delayed purchases before GST 2.0 took effect in September 2025. It calls this "the most base-distorted print of the year".

title: Archies' 'A Gift That Keeps Walking' Diwali film features a painted elephant
body: Archies launched a Diwali digital video campaign tied to Elephant Parade, an art brand and social enterprise focused on elephant welfare. The film follows a small grey baby elephant that comes alive as a diya flickers and ends as a painted sculpture given as a gift. The campaign also tells the story of Mosha, an elephant who lost part of her leg to a landmine and became "the first elephant in the world to walk on a prosthetic leg". It is built around a limited-edition collection. The page reports 457 views and no spend, reach or engagement data, so there is no sign yet of public debate.

title: Spotify's Diwali films with the Gullak cast extend its 'chores made fun' campaign
body: Spotify India launched three Diwali films with the cast of TVF's Gullak under the tagline "Diwali ki taiyaari fun banao, Spotify chalao". Each shows the Mishra family arguing over making laddoos, a rangoli, or tangled lights until someone plays music. The films run on Spotify's Instagram and YouTube channels and extend its earlier "Roz ke Kaam Fun Banao" campaign. Spotify says festive-season party playlist streams were up 34% and devotional listening up 13% versus the August baseline, reaching 5.24 million weekly content hours. The page carries no audience reaction.

title: Asian Paints' 'Taiyyari Shuru, Tyohaar Shuru' Diwali film
body: Asian Paints' Diwali film presents festive preparation as a celebration in itself. It focuses on repainting walls, adding care to small corners, and the family moments that make a home feel festive before the holiday. The Ads of the World page lists it only as published in India in October 2026, with no day printed. The date in this entry is therefore an approximation, and the page says it was submitted 7 days before capture. The page lists no agency or audience reaction.

title: InnoData lays off nearly 550 employees in India, logging them out mid-shift
body: India Today reported that InnoData cut nearly 550 employees in India on 26 October 2026, and the company has not confirmed the figure. Staff lost access to their official devices one by one mid-shift, and their IDs were deactivated before any formal notice. Termination emails reached personal accounts later and cited a reduction in the business assignment, not individual performance. Employees said HR had not contacted them, and they lost the payroll app before they could download payslips. By late evening a WhatsApp group of affected staff had almost 500 members, and one employee said the group was 'all clueless and in a state of panic.'

title: Microsoft India pay hikes disappoint: 91% got 5% or less, Blind survey says
body: A Blind survey of 2,178 India-based professionals found that 91% of Microsoft respondents received hikes of 5% or less in 2026, up from 45% in 2025. 86% said they were dissatisfied, and only 5% got more than 10%. Across India's tech workforce in the same survey, 35% reported no hike or a pay cut, and nearly two-thirds were unhappy with their increments. Respondents blamed company financial performance or cost-cutting most often (41%), then individual ratings (22%) and AI and automation priorities (18%). Blind searches by Indian users about buyouts and voluntary exits rose 60% over the past year. The page has no direct employee quotes.

title: Microsoft's voluntary exit offer leaves Indian employees rattled: 'Will we be sacked in 2027?'
body: About 60,000 Microsoft employees reportedly received a buyout offer, with payout of three months' pay for notice plus one month per year of service, and a year of health insurance. Acceptance is due by December 1, and four orgs were spared. A first-year employee asked, 'Will we be sacked early next year if we don't take the offer?' and warned, 'What if all of us accept the VEO? The entire org will collapse.' Her manager could not answer. Insiders said even vice-president-level staff were surprised. A Telangana Today piece dated 28 October adds that Hyderabad staff on Reddit are split. One said they felt less fear than expected, while a 29-year-old said they are burnt out and want a break to reset.

title: Barclays to cut about 5,000 roles on AI push; India back-office exposed
body: Barclays is cutting about 5,000 roles, nearly 5% of staff. About 1,000 jobs have already gone and 4,000 more are expected by the end of the year. About 60% of the cuts fall in support functions, including developer roles. The bank expects £1.1 billion in savings by 2027. Unions criticised it for using AI as a reason to cut jobs instead of reskilling staff. The article notes the cuts will affect Indian operations because many back-office functions are based in India.

title: Amazon's latest corporate layoffs reach India, workers worry about severance
body: Amazon cut fewer than 1,000 employees in its Stores division, with staff in the UK and India affected. This follows about 30,000 roles cut since late 2025 as spending shifts to AI, including $48 billion planned for India. Affected staff posted on an internal Slack channel that they had received emails citing 'the team's restructuring.' They voiced concern about severance pay and about internal job postings. India requires 3 months' written notice for establishments with more than 300 workers. Former employees estimate severance of one week of base pay per six months of service. Inc42 (9 Oct) reported at least 100 affected in India, and Amazon did not disclose an India number.

title: Wipro headcount falls by 6,716 in the September quarter
body: Wipro's headcount fell to 236,328 in Q2 FY27 from 243,044 in Q1, a drop of about 2.8%. It is still up 836 year on year. Net utilisation (excluding trainees) slipped to 83.4% from 86.4% a year earlier. Voluntary attrition eased to 13.8% from 13.9% in Q1. The article says the published data does not explain why headcount fell, and no breakdown of departures or restructuring was given. It also notes 93,994 employees completed Master AI certification as part of AI skilling. It quotes no employee reactions.

title: Q2 FY27: HCLTech, Infosys and TCS add staff, with fresher hiring rebounding at HCLTech
body: In the September quarter HCLTech added 6,450 people, reaching 2,30,339, and recruited 6,136 freshers, up from 1,056 the previous quarter. Infosys added 4,480 to reach 3,32,542, with voluntary attrition down to 12.7% from 13%. TCS stood at 5,98,056, up 4,258, with attrition at 13.3% and learning hours up 17%. The article calls it a mixed picture, not a sector-wide recovery. It cautions that a headcount drop does not necessarily mean people are leaving and that attrition definitions differ between firms. It quotes no employees.

title: Qualcomm to begin job cuts in November; number of roles undisclosed
body: Qualcomm plans job cuts starting in November 2026 and has not said how many roles are affected. It had about 52,000 employees globally as of September 2025. CEO Cristiano Amon's memo, reported by Reuters, said 'As we have expanded the business, so have the competencies and skills we require,' and that it needs 'the right people in the right roles.' The article does not say whether India staff are affected and quotes no employees or analysts. It is a thin report, but it adds to the sense of tech workers waiting for cuts.

title: Delhi-NCR offices told to run at 50% attendance from 5 November under pollution order
body: The Commission for Air Quality Management ordered government and private offices in Delhi and Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat, Ghaziabad and Gautam Buddha Nagar to allow 'no more than 50% of staff to attend physically.' The order, dated 30 October, runs from 5 November to 20 November. Industrial establishments and essential services where remote work is not feasible are exempt. The order cites CAQM's review of November air quality from 2018 to 2025, which showed recurring severe spikes. The article includes no reactions from companies or employees. It is the only work-from-home mandate in this set and comes from pollution, not company policy.

title: Noida labour officials call viral 'mandatory Rs 5,100 Diwali bonus' message false
body: A viral message claimed the Supreme Court had ordered a Rs 5,100 Diwali bonus for all government departments and private companies, payable by 5 November. Noida Additional Labour Commissioner Rakesh Dwivedi called it 'false and fabricated.' He said eligibility needs at least 30 days of work between April 2025 and March 2026 and a company at least five years old and profitable. The disbursement deadline is 30 November 2026, and police have registered an FIR. He urged workers not to protest over unverified reports. The article notes the rumours came about six months after Noida worker protests over minimum wage demands, which shows how much workers expect from festive pay.

title: BEST employees get Rs 33,000 Diwali bonus, up Rs 2,000 from last year
body: Mumbai's BEST undertaking announced a Rs 33,000 festive bonus for each of its 22,654 employees, about Rs 75 crore in total. It is Rs 2,000 more than last year and is credited to bank accounts on 3 November. BEST Committee Chairperson Trushna Vishwasrao made the announcement. The article quotes no workers or unions. It describes the payout as festive relief for staff who keep the city's buses running, which is the author's framing, not a quoted reaction. This is a public-sector item, a contrast to the squeezed pay hikes in private tech.

title: Google adds about 10,000 employees in six months, bucking tech layoff trend
body: Google's headcount reached 204,757 at the end of September 2026, up roughly 10,000 since March, per its Q3 results. Part of the rise comes from the Wiz acquisition, completed 11 March 2026, which brought about 2,000 employees. The article does not say how the growth splits between hiring and the acquisition. Quarterly revenue rose 25% year on year. It contrasts Google with Meta's repeated cost-cutting rounds and Microsoft's voluntary buyout. It has no India-specific data or employee reactions, so it is global context for Indian tech workers watching layoffs elsewhere.

title: Instagram tests 'Features' long-form video; Indian creators doubt it will pay
body: Instagram is testing 'Features', a widescreen long-video format, with a limited group of users in the US and some creators in Brazil. The page shows only 'November 2' as the date, and the year is inferred from the image path. It puts Instagram's India user base at more than 532 million. It estimates YouTube pays Rs 50 to Rs 200 per 1,000 long-form views, with a 55% creator share. Creator Larissa D'Sa says Instagram will struggle without clear revenue sharing and notes 'Capturing someone's attention for a few seconds is very different from keeping them engaged.' Others point to IGTV, which was discontinued in 2022, and expect creators to repost YouTube videos first.

title: Meta tests a Reels-first Facebook in India that opens straight into full-screen video
body: Meta is testing a Facebook layout in India that opens some users directly into full-screen video. Users in the test can opt out to a Feed-first view, and the classic feed stays as a second tab. The test also runs in Indonesia. The article says India is Facebook's largest market, with an audience of more than 400 million people according to Meta's ad tools. It cites a Meta-commissioned finding that 89% of Gen Z respondents use Reels every day. The page includes no independent user reaction.

title: Travel creator's reel of a 6'8" husband in an Air India washroom draws pushback
body: The travel couple @rayandramisa posted a light-hearted Instagram POV reel of the husband, who is 6'8", struggling to fit inside an Air India aircraft washroom. Many Indian users criticised it, saying Air India doesn't make its planes and that Boeing or Airbus builds them for many airlines. One commenter called it 'a dumb post', and another added a body-shaming remark. The clip has also started a wider conversation about lavatory size and passenger comfort. The page gives no view or like counts.

title: Delhi firm gifts staff iPhone 16s for Diwali, and the internet asks 'where do I apply?'
body: A Rohini, Delhi company posted a 15-second Instagram video of iPhone 16s in four colours on employees' desks as Diwali gifts. The caption read 'No competition. Aapko kya mila?' and invited people to share what they got. Some viewers asked whether the video was AI-generated, and the company replied that it wasn't and told them to watch again. Comments included 'any open positions?', a joke about avoiding Instagram to skip the envy, and one user saying they got no sweets from their employer. The page doesn't say what its '1K' figure measures.

title: Corporate Diwali gift reviews trend as Mumbai Central Line delays spark memes
body: Employees are posting reviews of the gifts their companies handed out, from lavish hampers to ones they found disrespectful. The article calls the reviews entertaining. The same roundup says the Mumbai Central Line suffered delays of over five hours from technical glitches. Commuters vented about ageing infrastructure, and reels spread with captions like 'the first in my bloodline to witness this.' The page gives no view or engagement numbers.

title: Saif Ali Khan's ghee joke from KBC becomes the month's biggest meme
body: The meme began on Kaun Banega Crorepati, where a tenth correct answer won a two-year supply of ghee. Saif later joked that he never received it. Gowardhan posted a video asking fans to move on, and Zomato joined in with Saif-themed puns on delivery bags. The same piece covers creators posting Instagram explainers on the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project in Arunachal Pradesh, an 11,200 MW dam. A 12-hour bandh was held against it on October 23. The page gives no sales or engagement figures for the ghee meme.

title: Vijay Deverakonda calls out online trolling and files a cyber complaint after Koffee With Karan
body: After Rashmika said on the show that she proposed 'nearly 100 times', many users labelled Vijay a 'red flag'. His team filed a complaint with Hyderabad cybercrime police over alleged fabricated content, manipulated screenshots, impersonation and harassment. Police have not yet confirmed the matter. Rashmika posted that the criticism felt like an angry mob and objected to comments about her family. Vijay posted a defence of his marriage on Instagram. The episode has become a row over how far online pile-ons can go.

title: Ramayana makers' trailer meme templates on X get a backlash
body: The film's official X handle posted meme templates made from the trailer ahead of its November 5 release. Many users said memes are the wrong tool for a story people hold in reverence, and some warned it could backfire on the makers. Others said fans will make their own memes anyway and the team should find a fresh way to engage the audience. The page says the timestamps are inconsistent and gives no engagement figures.

title: Soni Razdan says her 'anti-national' firecracker post was twisted
body: Actress Soni Razdan, 70, posted on Instagram that bursting even one cracker on Diwali is 'anti-life, anti-health and yes... anti-national.' Users criticised the 'anti-national' wording. On Thursday she wrote on X that people were trying to 'twist my post' and that her concern was air pollution, not religion. She said children deserve clean air. The date shown is the 'updated' time, and the page gives no engagement figures.

title: Stick-figure apocalypse reels, 'They have yet to comment' and 'See you in another story' take over feeds
body: Accounts posting stick figures surviving nuclear disasters and zombie apocalypses multiplied during the week, some as episodic reels and some with plots built from viewer responses. The 'They have yet to comment' trend mocks the habit of asking which celebrities have spoken up after a crisis while they stay silent on local issues. 'See you in another story' uses end-credits-style montages, which commenters call a year-ender template. The same roundup says users joked about 'National Slap Your Co-Worker Day', and some posted about being nice to avoid it. No figures are given.

title: Corporate Navratri, Beyblade Garba and 'Type C' personality posts trend with office-bound Indians
body: In 'Corporate Navratri', office employees bring garba into the workday because they can't go out to play. 'Beyblade Garba' shows dancers spinning rapidly in intricate routines. 'Type C' has users describe their own strengths and flaws as a personality outside the Type A and Type B boxes. The roundup also notes a 'fire transition' trend using sanitiser on a flame, which it calls risky. About 300 girls at Savitribai Phule Pune University marched to the police station over harassment near their hostel, and the university suspended two students. The page gives no engagement figures.

title: 'Yeh Muse hai kya?': Instagram users confused by Meta's AI agent, plus the AI Kitten Knight meme
body: Instagram users were shown Muse, Meta's AI agent. Many didn't know what it was for, and it isn't available in India, which added to the confusion. The week's other trends included recreating studio family portraits with friends at a photo studio. A small AI-generated kitten that fights dragons and warriors also went viral and became a meme about resilience. The 2025 'State Property' angry-grandpa meme returned in regional versions. The page gives no view or engagement figures.

title: Jailer 2 is in week 4 and still pulling in crowds after a huge run
body: Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 earned ₹3.00 Cr India net on Day 21 (Wed 4 Nov) across 8,004 shows. That was down 10.4% from Day 20's ₹3.35 Cr. After 21 days the page lists ₹466.05 Cr India net, ₹545.10 Cr India gross and ₹821.10 Cr worldwide gross. Day 21 occupancy averaged 12.0%, with Kannada highest at 21.0% and Hindi lowest at 8.0%. The page has no viewer quotes. The figures show a film that has become a long-running event, and other October releases have struggled to find screens next to it.

title: Sunday box office roundup: Aadarsha Kutumbam, Udta Teer and Drishyam: The Conclusion share a crowded weekend
body: The report covers Sunday 1 November. Aadarsha Kutumbam – House No. 47 took ₹11.25–11.50 crore India net, with a three-day India net of about ₹31.40 crore. Jailer 2 made ₹10.85–11.47 crore. Udta Teer made ₹4.12–4.40 crore, with a cumulative India net of about ₹41–42 crore. Drishyam: The Conclusion was at ₹375.60 crore India net through Saturday, in its fifth week. The page calls it 'a competitive Sunday' and says Drishyam 'continued to attract audiences'. The numbers are trade estimates and the page has no direct audience quotes.

title: Shilpa Rao's mic cut off mid-song at Bollywood Music Project; #JusticeForShilpaRao trends
body: At the 10th anniversary Bollywood Music Project in Mumbai on Saturday 24 October, Shilpa Rao's mic was switched off while she sang Chuttamalle from Devara: Part 1. She had waited for a replacement mic during sound problems. When she tried to thank the crowd, the next act, Kutle Khan and his band, began and interrupted her. Fans criticised the festival's management online and #JusticeForShilpaRao trended. Shilpa posted on Instagram: 'Our story tonight was left unfinished. I promise, I will come back.' Organisers apologised and blamed earlier sets running long and venue curfew rules. Some fans said better planning could have avoided it.

title: Daler Mehndi row: Abhijeet Bhattacharya says he will never lip-sync, backs the minister who questioned the show
body: An Uttarakhand minister, Subodh Uniyal, confronted Daler Mehndi mid-performance in October. He questioned whether the singer was really singing live and suggested he appeared drunk. At Chhattisgarh Rajyotsava 2026, Abhijeet Bhattacharya said of the minister: 'He spoke the truth. But he ended up becoming the villain in the eyes of many people.' He promised every note at his own shows would be live. Mika Singh defended his brother, saying he had been unwell, had recently had major surgery and never drank. Uniyal refused to apologise and noted Mehndi was paid Rs 35 lakh, arguing the audience did not get what it paid for. The row has turned into a wider argument about lip-syncing at paid concerts.

title: India crushed by 87 runs in Auckland as Phillips hits 107 off 49; Iyer says bowling fell short
body: In the 4th T20I at Eden Park on 30 October, New Zealand made 259/7 and won by 87 runs. Glenn Phillips scored 107 off 49 balls and Michael Bracewell 65 off 25. Phillips hit 32 runs off one Nitish Kumar Reddy over, and the pair hit 16 of New Zealand's 20 sixes. The margin was India's second-heaviest T20I defeat. India still led the series 3-1 at that point. Captain Shreyas Iyer said the bowling fell short, especially in the powerplay, and that the team must 'go back to the drawing board'. He also said the small ground was hard to adapt to. The page itself has no fan comments.

title: Drishyam 3: Hindi vs Malayalam – which version connected better with audiences?
body: The Hindi Drishyam 3 (released 2 October) is listed at ₹315.25 Cr India net and ₹489.74 Cr worldwide gross as of 11 days. The Malayalam film (released 21 May) is at ₹110.49 Cr India net and ₹239.83 Cr worldwide. Hindi viewers praised the suspense, the interval and the climax, and saw it as a satisfying close. Malayalam viewers praised Mohanlal's controlled performance and emotional weight, though some found the pacing slow and familiar. Both were faulted for leaning on familiar thriller devices. The article's own verdict is that the Hindi version 'appears to have satisfied more of the expectations' for a final chapter. The page offers no survey data.

title: Ramayana Part 1 opens: ₹26.44 Cr India net live estimate on Day 1
body: Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana Part 1 opened on 5 November. The live estimate at 2:03 PM IST was ₹26.44 Cr India net and ₹31.20 Cr India gross across 13,010 shows, with overall occupancy of 26.8%. Hindi made ₹19.27 Cr, Kannada ₹3.22 Cr, Telugu ₹2.53 Cr, Tamil ₹97 L and Malayalam ₹45 L. The page says these numbers are still updating. It notes the music has drawn 'divided reactions'. Audience verdicts were still coming in at the time of the page.

title: Ramayana first reactions: 'breathtaking visuals', 'emotionally flat' and a score that divides viewers
body: Early social-media reactions came from an LA premiere of the English-dubbed 3D cut, about 30 minutes shorter than the Hindi version. The Hindi version runs 195 minutes. Yash got strong praise as Ravana, and Ranbir Kapoor's restrained Ram and Sai Pallavi's Sita were also liked. Some viewers called select sequences breathtaking, while others found parts synthetic. The writing was called sluggish and the AR Rahman–Hans Zimmer score drew criticism. The common view was 'ambitious but uneven'. Full critic reviews were still under embargo at the time.

title: Vijay Deverakonda's Ranabaali: ₹52.55 Cr India gross in week 1, but can it avoid a loss?
body: Ranabaali's week 1 was ₹52.55 Cr India gross and ₹63.65 Cr worldwide, against a reported budget of about ₹120 Cr. The pre-release estimate of theatrical break-even was about ₹60-65 Cr in distributor share. Day 1 was ₹10.75 Cr, falling to ₹3.65 Cr on Day 7. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana gave ₹44.75 Cr (85.2%), and Tamil Nadu only ₹0.90 Cr. Occupancy fell to 31% by Thursday even with more than 2,100 shows still on. The festive boost on Tuesday faded afterwards. The article reads this as weak turnout, not a screen shortage.

title: Ayushmann Khurrana's Udta Teer opens at ₹4.10 Cr, short of his top openers
body: Udta Teer made ₹4.10 Cr India net on Friday 23 October, the eighth best opening of Ayushmann's career. That is far behind Thamma's ₹24.00 Cr. It ran in 6,265 shows at 13% occupancy, with 1,87,849 footfalls. The page says it 'struggled to generate strong initial demand'. It blames limited pre-release buzz, an unconventional spy-comedy premise and competition from Jailer 2. The film later grew over the weekend, and the 1 November roundup puts its cumulative India net at about ₹41–42 crore.

title: Akka review: Radhika Apte and Keerthy Suresh rule the screen, but the Netflix series falls short
body: Netflix's Akka premiered on 30 October. It is set in Pernuru, a fictional kingdom ruled by women, with Keerthy Suresh as Bhavani Akka and Radhika Apte as Rudra. The review praises the two leads as the strongest reason to watch. It faults the unclear focus, weak pacing, disjointed edit and rushed ending. It says the show 'settles for a gender-swapped gangster drama instead of challenging the genre' and calls it 'a series with the personality of cardboard'. The series was reportedly ready in 2024 and reshot several times, with gory scenes cut. This is a critic's view, not audience data.

title: Matargashti on Netflix: a warm Lucknow father-daughter dramedy
body: Matargashti is a five-episode Netflix series, with episodes under 25 minutes. It is set in Lucknow. Adrija Sinha plays Dhara, a studious teenager, and Rajesh Kumar plays her anxious single father, Prakash. Reviewer Rahul Desai calls it warm and watchable, with a low-key take on girlhood and no sensationalism. He says it explores grief, distance between parent and child, and how control can look like care. The review describes these themes as authentic but not especially comfortable. It reads as a small, relatable show for family viewing.

title: Annual FASTag local pass starts 1 November for people living near toll plazas
body: From 1 November 2026, private vehicle owners living within 20 km of a National Highway fee plaza can buy a concessional annual FASTag local pass. It costs ₹1,500 for plazas outside municipal limits and ₹3,000 for plazas within them. The current monthly local pass costs ₹360, or ₹4,320 a year, so the cheaper annual pass can save ₹2,820. Living nearby does not automatically qualify you. The pass is not available on closed-toll expressways or where a service road exists. Vehicles without a valid FASTag pay 1.25 times the fee via UPI, or double in cash. The page quotes no public reaction.

title: Is rent the new dealbreaker? Young professionals weigh offers against housing costs
body: A 23-year-old, Ridhima Gupta, turned down a Rs 60,000 monthly job offer in Lower Parel after finding a basic 1BHK nearby cost Rs 50,000 to Rs 60,000. Knight Frank data for H1 2026 shows Mumbai Metropolitan Region and NCR above 50% of household income going to home-loan EMIs. Ahmedabad is at 23%, Kolkata 25% and Pune 28%. An HR head said, 'For Gen Z and millennials, the offer letter now has to be read alongside the rent receipt.' Mansi Tyagi, who moved to Mumbai from Bareilly, says she is counting every rupee by the third week of the month, but stays.

title: What changes on 1 November: pension life certificates, ITR deadline, GST tweaks
body: Pensioners below 80 can submit life certificates from 1 November, generally until 30 November. Missing the deadline could temporarily stop pension payments. For specified audited taxpayers, the AY 2026-27 return deadline moved from October 31 to November 21, 2026. The extension does not cover all taxpayers, so salaried people should check their own date. A Cabinet-approved disability pension reform would lower the minimum disability threshold from 80% to 40%, but it is not expected to start on 1 November. The page gave no LPG figure and quotes no public reaction.

title: Urban India heads into Diwali with a smaller wallet
body: A LocalCircles survey of 67,000+ responses puts total urban festive spending at ₹1.97 lakh crore, down 6% from ₹2.10 lakh crore in 2025. Urban households plan to spend about ₹20,000 each, and 31% plan no discretionary festive purchase. No-cost EMIs make up about 50% of Amazon purchases, up from 30%, and 83% of households planning purchases expect to use savings. Retail inflation was 5.54% in September. The article's view is that shoppers are still turning up but 'buying cheaper things, fewer phones, and paying with savings and EMIs'.

title: Airlines schedule 2.6% fewer domestic flights for the November festival period as fares bite
body: Weekly domestic flights fall from 22,912 in October 2025 to 22,306 this November, a drop of 606. Air India cut 543 weekly flights (14.9%), and IndiGo is down 375 (2.7%). Patna's weekly departures fell nearly 20%, from 377 to 302, and Hyderabad-Patna dropped from 90 to 42 weekly flights. The article blames higher aviation fuel costs and rupee depreciation. IndiGo CEO Willie Walsh said domestic festival demand remained strong. The article compares different months and years, so treat the comparison loosely.

title: New aviation rules: airlines must show full fare breakdown, government can step in on fares
body: The Civil Aviation Ministry notified the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam 2026, which replaces the Aircraft Rules of 1937 from the start of 2027. Booking platforms must break the total into service-provider fees, operating costs and government taxes, and show the total payable during booking and on the ticket. Airlines must disclose cancellation charges and refund conditions. Rule 192 has the DGCA monitor tariffs, and the Centre can order temporary fare changes in the public interest. The article says transparency may let people compare airlines but may not lower fares. It quotes no passenger or industry reactions.

title: Retail inflation jumps to 5.54% in September as onions more than double
body: Retail inflation was 5.54% in September 2026, up from 4.83% in August, and food inflation rose to 7.74%. Onion inflation hit 108.09%, ginger 62.85%, garlic 54.62% and lemons 36.41%. Potatoes were down 11.50% and tomatoes down 8.62%. Rural inflation was 6.08% against 4.88% in urban areas. Tamil Nadu was highest among major states at 6.81% and Delhi lowest at 3.40%. The page is a data report and quotes no household reactions.

title: Commercial LPG rises again before Diwali; household cylinder price unchanged
body: From 1 November 2026 the 19 kg commercial cylinder rose by Rs 10 to Rs 17 across metros, to Rs 2,820 in Delhi and Rs 2,775 in Mumbai. The 14.2 kg domestic cylinder is unchanged at Rs 942 in Delhi, Rs 941.50 in Mumbai and Rs 968 in Kolkata. Domestic prices have not moved since 7 June 2026, when they rose by Rs 29. The page quotes no reactions. Commercial gas feeds restaurant and street-food costs, so it matters to people who eat out.

title: Gold ahead of Dhanteras: Rs 1.47 lakh per 10 grams for 24K in Mumbai and Delhi
body: Indicative retail rates on 18 October 2026 were Rs 1,47,660 for 24K and Rs 1,35,350 for 22K per 10 grams in Mumbai. Delhi was Rs 1,47,810 for 24K and Rs 1,35,500 for 22K. These exclude GST and making charges. The Upstox piece says Mumbai gold rose from about ₹93,000 to roughly ₹1.5 lakh between April 2025 and October 2026. The page itself quotes no buyer reactions. It is a rate table, not a report on what shoppers said.

title: Caller name display from 1 November and new TRAI spam-call rules rolling out
body: The DoT directs operators to show the caller's name (CNAP) on 4G and higher networks from 1 November 2026. Stage 1 of TRAI's amended calling rules went live around 18 October. Enquiry leads get a seven-day window, and transaction-support calls need explicit consent. Stage 2, covering automated-call declarations, is due around 17 November. The page says its own dates are estimates. It is an industry blog and quotes no consumer reactions.

title: EPFO tests UPI-based PF withdrawals, launch likely by December
body: EPFO has begun testing UPI-based EPF withdrawals with banks, and the formal launch is expected by the end of December 2026. Under existing rules, up to 75% of the eligible balance can be withdrawn and 25% must stay in the account earning tax-free interest. The page cites about 300 million subscribers, about 7.5 crore active contributors and a corpus close to ₹26 lakh crore. The article quotes no subscriber reactions. Earlier launch targets slipped.

title: RBI raises repo rate 25 bps to 5.50%, so floating-rate EMIs may rise
body: The RBI's MPC raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% on 7 October 2026. The vote was unanimous and the stance changed to 'calibrated tightening'. The standing deposit facility rate is 5.25% and the MSF and Bank Rate are 5.75%. Floating-rate home, personal and auto loans linked to EBLR or MCLR are most affected, while fixed-rate loans are not. Depositors may see slightly better FD rates over time. The source is a loan marketplace and quotes no borrower reactions.
